raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
This PR makes CPU initialization of MoE experts independent of the expert-parallel layout. Currently, EP=4 with eight experts produces only two distinct initial expert weights because each EP rank draws from the same CPU RNG stream.

The change introduces per-global-expert CPU RNG streams, preserves distinct draws for FC1 and FC2, and prevents expert initialization from advancing the shared RNG differently across layouts. TE grouped and duplicated linear layers initialize full logical weights before applying ETP/GTP sharding.

Validation:

- 51 targeted tests passed on four GB300 GPUs using PyTorch 26.07 and TE 2.19.
- Coverage includes grouped/sequential experts, EP/ETP/GTP layout invariance, BF16/MXFP8 initialization, and RNG restoration.
- Reproduced duplicate experts on latest main in both expert implementations.
- Formatting and Ruff checks passed.

CPU initialization with moe_single_grouped_weight=True remains explicitly unsupported. Full CI validation with the current container remains pending.

<!-- nemo-ci-review-impact:v1 ceiling=moderate -->

Completed the light review of all seven changed files and their directly affected initialization paths. Static review only; tests were not executed.

### [P2] Preserve gate/up pairing when CPU-sharding grouped FC1

The new [grouped CPU initializer](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5f438f645bdf1d89e49335d912566b1a4f5e8d7a/megatron/core/extensions/transformer_engine.py#L2882-L2906) always uses `stride=1`. With `gated_linear_unit=True`, no GLU interleaving, and ETP=2, this gives rank 0 the first contiguous half of FC1—only gate rows—and rank 1 only up rows. Each rank nevertheless [splits its local activation into gate/up halves](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5f438f645bdf1d89e49335d912566b1a4f5e8d7a/megatron/core/transformer/moe/experts.py#L1172-L1179). Consequently, the same seed initializes a different logical expert at ETP=1 versus ETP=2. For a logical FC1 `[G0,G1,U0,U1]`, the expected local weights are `[G0,U0]` and `[G1,U1]`, not `[G0,G1]` and `[U0,U1]`.

**Correction:** In `TEGroupedLinear.__init__`, select stride 2 only for non-interleaved gated column weights, and keep the CPU parameter's partition metadata consistent. Suggested patch for that new initialization block:

```diff
-                with expert_cpu_init_scope():
+                cpu_init_stride = (
+                    2
+                    if original_parallel_mode == "column"
+                    and config.gated_linear_unit
+                    and config.moe_mlp_glu_interleave_size is None
+                    else 1
+                )
+                with expert_cpu_init_scope():
                     for local_expert_idx in range(num_gemms):
                         weight = getattr(self, f"weight{local_expert_idx}")
+                        weight.partition_stride = cpu_init_stride
@@
-                                stride=1,
+                                stride=cpu_init_stride,
```

**Preservation:** Nongated FC1 must retain contiguous output-row partitions; FC2 must retain contiguous input-column partitions even when GLU is enabled. Explicitly interleaved GLU weights must also retain contiguous partitions—the [interleaving resolver](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5f438f645bdf1d89e49335d912566b1a4f5e8d7a/megatron/core/transformer/moe/experts.py#L988-L994) expects paired interleaved blocks, not two global halves. Keep GPU initialization, per-global-expert streams, full logical RNG draws, and subsequent GTP slicing unchanged.

**Acceptance — proposed checks:** Extend the [layout regression](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5f438f645bdf1d89e49335d912566b1a4f5e8d7a/tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_expert_cpu_init.py#L180-L204), which currently leaves GLU disabled. Using eight experts, hidden size 128, FFN size 256, and gated SiLU, compare ETP=2 against ETP=1: each local FC1 must equal the concatenation of that rank's slice of the reference gate half and its slice of the up half; FC2 must equal the corresponding reference input-column slice. Repeat with nongated FC1 and with interleave size 32, expecting contiguous FC1 slices instead. Retain the existing nongated layout comparisons and the [distinct successive draws/shared-RNG-tail assertions](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5f438f645bdf1d89e49335d912566b1a4f5e8d7a/tests/unit_tests/tensor_parallel/test_expert_cpu_rng.py#L30-L44). Verify the suggested patch before adoption.

### [P3] Include the new MXFP8 regression cases in GB200 CI selection

The added [duplicated-linear tests](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5f438f645bdf1d89e49335d912566b1a4f5e8d7a/tests/unit_tests/generalized_tensor_parallel/test_gtp_cpu_init.py#L288-L295) include MXFP8 cases, but this file has no `launch_on_gb200` marker. H100 skips those cases through `_requires_mxfp8`; meanwhile, the [GB200 file selector](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5f438f645bdf1d89e49335d912566b1a4f5e8d7a/tests/unit_tests/find_test_cases.py#L89-L98) excludes unmarked files, and its [pytest invocation also selects that marker](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5f438f645bdf1d89e49335d912566b1a4f5e8d7a/tests/unit_tests/run_ci_test.sh#L114-L117). Thus the new quantized initialization regression is not exercised by either hardware lane.

**Correction:** Add this module-level declaration after the imports in the GTP CPU-init test file:

```python
pytestmark = pytest.mark.launch_on_gb200
```

This retains H100 BF16 coverage, existing hardware/version skips, and all parameter combinations; the GB200 marker is additive on H100.

**Acceptance — proposed checks:** On a GTP-capable environment, collecting this file with `pytest --collect-only -m launch_on_gb200` should include all 11 cases, including both new `fp8_param=True` duplicated-linear cases. The GB200 file selector must no longer emit an ignore entry for this file. Execute those MXFP8 cases on Blackwell and retain their exact equality assertion against GTP=1.

> **Note:** formal approval is not available for this request, so this review is posted as a comment only.

*Review generated by codex. This was a full review. Request a full review with `/review reset=true`.*

[P3] Use double quotes in the new process-group list

These new literals use single quotes, contrary to the repository's [explicit string convention](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ede2c586cf70dd452f93b9726b31cbedc8df0dd0/style-guide.md#L9-L10), which Black intentionally does not enforce. Replace only the quoting, retaining every requested group and its order:

```suggestion
        required_pgs=["tp", "cp", "pp", "ep", "expt_tp", "gtp_remat", "expt_gtp_remat"]
```

Static acceptance: all seven names remain unchanged and use double-quoted literals. This is style-only; no runtime behavior should change.

+"""``use_cpu_initialization`` must build the same global expert stack at every EP degree.
+
+CPU initialization exists so a run's initial weights are a function of the seed alone, not of the
+parallel layout. Expert weights are the case that is easy to get wrong: the expert-parallel RNG
+separation lives in the **CUDA** tracker (``expert_parallel_seed`` folds in ``ep_rank``), which the
+plain CPU generator never sees. Without a per-expert CPU stream every EP rank initializes its local
+experts from the same draws, so a model with ``num_experts`` experts silently ends up holding only
+``num_experts // ep_size`` distinct ones -- correct shapes, correct dtypes, no crash, wrong model.
+
+Both expert implementations are covered because they reach the CPU path differently:
+``SequentialMLP`` goes through ``_initialize_affine_weight_cpu`` via one Linear per expert, while
+``TEGroupedLinear`` holds ``weight0..weightN-1`` in a single module.
+"""
+

+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist

+from megatron.core.process_groups_config import ProcessGroupCollection

+from megatron.core.transformer.transformer_config import TransformerConfig

+from tests.unit_tests.test_utilities import Utils
+

+NUM_EXPERTS = 8
+HIDDEN = 128
+FFN = 256
+SEED = 1234
+DTYPE = torch.bfloat16

+        num_layers=1,
+        hidden_size=HIDDEN,
+        num_attention_heads=8,
+        ffn_hidden_size=FFN,
+        num_moe_experts=NUM_EXPERTS,

+        moe_grouped_gemm=grouped,

+        params_dtype=DTYPE,

+        attention_dropout=0.0,
+        bias_dropout_fusion=False,
+        expert_model_parallel_size=ep,
+        expert_tensor_parallel_size=etp,

+        use_cpu_initialization=True,
+        init_method_std=0.02,

+
+def _build(ep, grouped, etp=1, egtp=1):
+    """Re-initialize model parallelism at this EP degree and build a CPU-initialized block."""
+    ps.destroy_model_parallel()
+    ps.initialize_model_parallel(

+    # is seeded too so a weight that falls back to GPU init is not silently skipped.
+    torch.manual_seed(SEED)

+# CPU initialization draws from the plain CPU generator, which -- unlike the CUDA tracker -- has no
+# expert-parallel term. Without a per-expert stream every EP rank would initialize its local experts
+# from the same draws, leaving only ``num_experts // ep_size`` distinct experts: right shapes, right
+# dtypes, no crash, wrong model.
+_EXPERT_CPU_INIT_SALT: Optional[int] = None
+_EXPERT_CPU_INIT_INDEX: Optional[int] = None
+_EXPERT_CPU_INIT_RNG_STATE: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+# Odd multiplier spreading adjacent expert indices across the seed space.
+_EXPERT_SEED_STRIDE = 7919
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def expert_cpu_init_scope(enabled: bool = True):
+    """Open a per-module salt for CPU-initialized expert weights.
+
+    Enter **once per expert-weight module**, around the loop over local experts. The single draw it
+    takes from the shared stream is what keeps otherwise-identical weights apart: without it, layer
+    0's expert *k* and layer 1's expert *k* have the same shape and the same seed, so they come out
+    with identical values.
+
+    The draw must happen per module and **not** per expert: it advances the shared stream, so once
+    per module advances it equally on every rank, whereas once per *local* expert would advance it
+    by ``num_experts // ep_size`` -- a rank-dependent amount that breaks layout invariance.
+    """
+    global _EXPERT_CPU_INIT_SALT
+    if not enabled:
+        yield
+        return
+    previous = _EXPERT_CPU_INIT_SALT
+    _EXPERT_CPU_INIT_SALT = int(torch.randint(0, 2**62, (1,)).item())
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        _EXPERT_CPU_INIT_SALT = previous
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def expert_cpu_init_index(global_expert_index: Optional[int]):
+    """Declare which GLOBAL expert the modules built inside this block belong to.
+
+    Paired with the enclosing :func:`expert_cpu_init_scope` salt by :func:`expert_cpu_init_rng`, so
+    the values an expert gets do not depend on which EP rank happens to own it. GPU initialization
+    ignores both: the CUDA tracker already folds in ``ep_rank``.
+    """
+    global _EXPERT_CPU_INIT_INDEX, _EXPERT_CPU_INIT_RNG_STATE
+    previous = _EXPERT_CPU_INIT_INDEX, _EXPERT_CPU_INIT_RNG_STATE
+    _EXPERT_CPU_INIT_INDEX = global_expert_index
+    _EXPERT_CPU_INIT_RNG_STATE = None
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        _EXPERT_CPU_INIT_INDEX, _EXPERT_CPU_INIT_RNG_STATE = previous
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def expert_cpu_init_rng():
+    """Run one CPU weight init on the enclosing global expert's stream, if there is one.
+
+    A no-op unless both context managers above are active. Inside them the CPU generator is switched
+    to a per-(module, expert) stream and **restored afterwards**, so expert initialization consumes
+    none of the shared stream -- otherwise layouts with a different number of local experts would
+    desync every weight built after the MoE layer. Only the CPU generator is touched:
+    ``torch.manual_seed`` would also reseed every CUDA generator, which this cannot restore.
+    """
+    global _EXPERT_CPU_INIT_RNG_STATE
+    global_expert_index, salt = _EXPERT_CPU_INIT_INDEX, _EXPERT_CPU_INIT_SALT
+    if global_expert_index is None or salt is None:
+        yield
+        return
+    cpu_rng_state = torch.get_rng_state()
+    try:
+        if _EXPERT_CPU_INIT_RNG_STATE is None:
+            seed = (salt + global_expert_index * _EXPERT_SEED_STRIDE) % (2**63 - 1)
+            torch.default_generator.manual_seed(seed)
+        else:
+            torch.set_rng_state(_EXPERT_CPU_INIT_RNG_STATE)
+        yield
+    finally:
+        # SequentialMLP builds FC1 and FC2 within one expert index. Continue its stream
+        # across weights instead of initializing both from the same random draws.
+        _EXPERT_CPU_INIT_RNG_STATE = torch.get_rng_state()
+        torch.set_rng_state(cpu_rng_state)
+

+"""Expert CPU streams must be independent without perturbing later dense weights."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.layers import _initialize_affine_weight_cpu
+from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.random import expert_cpu_init_index, expert_cpu_init_scope
+
+
+def _weight():
+    weight = torch.empty(16, 16)
+    _initialize_affine_weight_cpu(
+        weight, 16, 16, 16, 0, torch.nn.init.normal_, rank=0, world_size=1
+    )
+    return weight
+
+
+def _experts(indices):
+    torch.manual_seed(1234)
+    result = {}
+    with expert_cpu_init_scope():
+        for index in indices:
+            with expert_cpu_init_index(index):
+                result[index] = (_weight(), _weight())
+    return result, torch.rand(16)
+
+
+def test_successive_expert_weights_use_different_draws():
+    experts, _ = _experts([0, 1])
+    for fc1, fc2 in experts.values():
+        assert not torch.equal(fc1, fc2), "FC1 and FC2 restart the same CPU RNG stream"
+
+
+def test_expert_streams_are_layout_invariant():
+    reference, reference_tail = _experts(range(8))
+    for indices in (range(4), range(4, 8), range(6, 8)):
+        actual, tail = _experts(indices)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(tail, reference_tail, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        for index, weights in actual.items():
+            for actual_weight, expected_weight in zip(weights, reference[index]):
+                torch.testing.assert_close(actual_weight, expected_weight, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    assert not torch.equal(reference[0][0], reference[1][0])
+
+
+def test_expert_rng_restored_after_exception():
+    torch.manual_seed(1234)
+    with expert_cpu_init_scope():
+        shared_state = torch.get_rng_state().clone()
+        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="init failed"):
+            with expert_cpu_init_index(0):
+
+                def fail(weight):
+                    weight.normal_()
+                    raise RuntimeError("init failed")
+
+                _initialize_affine_weight_cpu(
+                    torch.empty(16, 16), 16, 16, 16, 0, fail, rank=0, world_size=1
+                )
+        assert torch.equal(torch.get_rng_state(), shared_state)
+    assert torch.equal(torch.get_rng_state(), shared_state)

+# Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+
+"""``use_cpu_initialization`` must build the same global expert stack at every EP degree.
+
+CPU initialization exists so a run's initial weights are a function of the seed alone, not of the
+parallel layout. Expert weights are the case that is easy to get wrong: the expert-parallel RNG
+separation lives in the **CUDA** tracker (``expert_parallel_seed`` folds in ``ep_rank``), which the
+plain CPU generator never sees. Without a per-expert CPU stream every EP rank initializes its local
+experts from the same draws, so a model with ``num_experts`` experts silently ends up holding only
+``num_experts // ep_size`` distinct ones -- correct shapes, correct dtypes, no crash, wrong model.
+
+Both expert implementations are covered because they reach the CPU path differently:
+``SequentialMLP`` goes through ``_initialize_affine_weight_cpu`` via one Linear per expert, while
+``TEGroupedLinear`` holds ``weight0..weightN-1`` in a single module.
+"""
+
+import hashlib
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+from megatron.core import parallel_state as ps
+from megatron.core.models.gpt.gpt_layer_specs import get_gpt_layer_with_transformer_engine_spec
+from megatron.core.process_groups_config import ProcessGroupCollection
+from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.random import model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed
+from megatron.core.transformer.transformer_block import TransformerBlock
+from megatron.core.transformer.transformer_config import TransformerConfig
+from megatron.core.utils import get_pg_rank
+from tests.unit_tests.test_utilities import Utils
+
+WORLD = 4
+NUM_EXPERTS = 8
+HIDDEN = 128
+FFN = 256
+SEED = 1234
+DTYPE = torch.bfloat16
+
+
+def _config(ep, grouped, etp=1, egtp=1):
+    return TransformerConfig(
+        num_layers=1,
+        hidden_size=HIDDEN,
+        num_attention_heads=8,
+        ffn_hidden_size=FFN,
+        num_moe_experts=NUM_EXPERTS,
+        moe_router_topk=2,
+        moe_grouped_gemm=grouped,
+        add_bias_linear=False,
+        params_dtype=DTYPE,
+        bf16=True,
+        hidden_dropout=0.0,
+        attention_dropout=0.0,
+        bias_dropout_fusion=False,
+        expert_model_parallel_size=ep,
+        expert_tensor_parallel_size=etp,
+        expert_gtp_weight_remat_size=egtp,
+        use_cpu_initialization=True,
+        init_method_std=0.02,
+    )
+
+
+def _build(ep, grouped, etp=1, egtp=1):
+    """Re-initialize model parallelism at this EP degree and build a CPU-initialized block."""
+    ps.destroy_model_parallel()
+    ps.initialize_model_parallel(
+        tensor_model_parallel_size=1,
+        pipeline_model_parallel_size=1,
+        expert_model_parallel_size=ep,
+        expert_tensor_parallel_size=etp,
+        expert_gtp_remat_size=egtp,
+    )
+    # CPU init draws from the CPU generator, which every rank seeds identically; the CUDA tracker
+    # is seeded too so a weight that falls back to GPU init is not silently skipped.
+    torch.manual_seed(SEED)
+    model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed(SEED, force_reset_rng=True)
+    pg_collection = ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups(
+        required_pgs=['tp', 'cp', 'pp', 'ep', 'expt_tp', 'gtp_remat', 'expt_gtp_remat']
+    )
+    spec = get_gpt_layer_with_transformer_engine_spec(
+        num_experts=NUM_EXPERTS, moe_grouped_gemm=grouped
+    )
+    block = TransformerBlock(
+        _config(ep, grouped, etp, egtp), spec, pg_collection=pg_collection
+    ).cuda()
+    return block, pg_collection
+
+
+def _global_digest(block, pg_collection, ep):
+    """name -> checksum for the whole model, keyed so layouts are comparable.
+
+    Local expert indices are rewritten to global ones (``weight3`` / ``local_experts.3`` ->
+    ``#e{ep_rank * num_local + 3}``) and every rank's entries are merged, so the result describes
+    the global model rather than one rank's slice of it.
+    """
+    import re
+
+    ep_rank = get_pg_rank(pg_collection.ep)
+    num_local = NUM_EXPERTS // ep
+    local = {}
+    for name, param in block.named_parameters():
+        grouped_match = re.search(r"(weight|bias)(\d+)$", name)
+        sequential_match = re.search(r"local_experts\.(\d+)\.", name)
+        if grouped_match:
+            index = ep_rank * num_local + int(grouped_match.group(2))
+            key = name[: grouped_match.start()] + f"{grouped_match.group(1)}#e{index}"
+        elif sequential_match:
+            index = ep_rank * num_local + int(sequential_match.group(1))
+            key = (
+                name[: sequential_match.start()]
+                + f"local_experts.#e{index}."
+                + name[sequential_match.end() :]
+            )
+        else:
+            key = name
+        values = param.data.detach().float()
+        if getattr(param, "gtp_remat_size", 1) > 1:
+            shards = [torch.empty_like(values) for _ in range(pg_collection.expt_gtp_remat.size())]
+            dist.all_gather(shards, values, group=pg_collection.expt_gtp_remat)
+            values = torch.cat(shards, dim=0)
+            pad_length = getattr(param, "pad_length", 0)
+            if pad_length:
+                values = values[:-pad_length]
+        if "#e" in key and pg_collection.expt_tp.size() > 1:
+            shards = [torch.empty_like(values) for _ in range(pg_collection.expt_tp.size())]
+            dist.all_gather(shards, values, group=pg_collection.expt_tp)
+            values = torch.cat(shards, dim=param.partition_dim)
+        values = values.cpu().contiguous()
+        local[key] = (tuple(values.shape), hashlib.sha256(values.numpy().tobytes()).hexdigest())
+
+    gathered = [None] * dist.get_world_size()
+    dist.all_gather_object(gathered, local)
+    merged = {}
+    for rank_digest in gathered:
+        for key, value in rank_digest.items():
+            if key in merged:
+                assert merged[key] == value, f"replicas disagree for {key}"
+            merged[key] = value
+    return merged
+
+
+def _expert_weight_keys(digest):
+    return [k for k in digest if "#e" in k and "fc1" in k]
+
+
+def _require_world():
+    """Skip unless this is a WORLD-rank torchrun job, bringing the process group up if needed.
+
+    Initialize before querying world size. Multiples of four also run these cases in the
+    eight-rank CI job instead of silently skipping them.
+    """
+    if torch.cuda.device_count() < WORLD:
+        pytest.skip(f"requires {WORLD} GPUs")
+    if not dist.is_initialized():
+        Utils.initialize_distributed()
+    if dist.get_world_size() % WORLD:
+        pytest.skip(f"requires world_size divisible by {WORLD}")
+
+
+class TestExpertCpuInitialization:
+    """CPU-initialized experts must not depend on the expert-parallel layout."""
+
+    def teardown_method(self, method):
+        Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("grouped", [True, False])
+    def test_experts_are_distinct(self, grouped):
+        """Every global expert must get its own values, not one draw shared across EP ranks."""
+        _require_world()
+        block, pg_collection = _build(WORLD, grouped)
+        digest = _global_digest(block, pg_collection, WORLD)
+        expert_keys = _expert_weight_keys(digest)
+        assert len(expert_keys) == NUM_EXPERTS, f"expected {NUM_EXPERTS} experts, got {expert_keys}"
+        distinct = {digest[k] for k in expert_keys}
+        assert len(distinct) == NUM_EXPERTS, (
+            f"only {len(distinct)} distinct experts out of {NUM_EXPERTS}: every EP rank drew the "
+            "same values (the CPU generator carries no expert-parallel term)"
+        )
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("grouped", [True, False])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        "ep,etp,egtp", [(2, 1, 1), (4, 1, 1), (2, 2, 1), (1, 4, 1), (2, 1, 2), (1, 1, 4)]
+    )
+    def test_global_model_matches_ep1(self, ep, etp, egtp, grouped):
+        """The whole model, experts included, must be bit-identical to the EP=1 build."""
+        _require_world()
+        reference_block, reference_pgs = _build(1, grouped)
+        reference = _global_digest(reference_block, reference_pgs, 1)
+        del reference_block
+
+        block, pg_collection = _build(ep, grouped, etp, egtp)
+        actual = _global_digest(block, pg_collection, ep)
+        del block
+
+        assert set(actual) == set(reference), (
+            f"EP={ep} and EP=1 disagree on which parameters exist: "
+            f"{sorted(set(actual) ^ set(reference))[:5]}"
+        )
+        differing = [k for k in sorted(reference) if reference[k] != actual[k]]
+        assert (
+            not differing
+        ), f"EP={ep} init differs from EP=1 for {len(differing)} params, e.g. " + "; ".join(
+            f"{k}: {reference[k]} vs {actual[k]}" for k in differing[:3]
+        )

<!-- nemo-ci-review-impact:v1 ceiling=moderate -->

Completed the light review of all seven changed files and their directly affected initialization paths. Static review only; tests were not executed.

### [P2] Preserve gate/up pairing when CPU-sharding grouped FC1

The new [grouped CPU initializer](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5f438f645bdf1d89e49335d912566b1a4f5e8d7a/megatron/core/extensions/transformer_engine.py#L2882-L2906) always uses `stride=1`. With `gated_linear_unit=True`, no GLU interleaving, and ETP=2, this gives rank 0 the first contiguous half of FC1—only gate rows—and rank 1 only up rows. Each rank nevertheless [splits its local activation into gate/up halves](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5f438f645bdf1d89e49335d912566b1a4f5e8d7a/megatron/core/transformer/moe/experts.py#L1172-L1179). Consequently, the same seed initializes a different logical expert at ETP=1 versus ETP=2. For a logical FC1 `[G0,G1,U0,U1]`, the expected local weights are `[G0,U0]` and `[G1,U1]`, not `[G0,G1]` and `[U0,U1]`.

**Correction:** In `TEGroupedLinear.__init__`, select stride 2 only for non-interleaved gated column weights, and keep the CPU parameter's partition metadata consistent. Suggested patch for that new initialization block:

```diff
-                with expert_cpu_init_scope():
+                cpu_init_stride = (
+                    2
+                    if original_parallel_mode == "column"
+                    and config.gated_linear_unit
+                    and config.moe_mlp_glu_interleave_size is None
+                    else 1
+                )
+                with expert_cpu_init_scope():
                     for local_expert_idx in range(num_gemms):
                         weight = getattr(self, f"weight{local_expert_idx}")
+                        weight.partition_stride = cpu_init_stride
@@
-                                stride=1,
+                                stride=cpu_init_stride,
```

**Preservation:** Nongated FC1 must retain contiguous output-row partitions; FC2 must retain contiguous input-column partitions even when GLU is enabled. Explicitly interleaved GLU weights must also retain contiguous partitions—the [interleaving resolver](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5f438f645bdf1d89e49335d912566b1a4f5e8d7a/megatron/core/transformer/moe/experts.py#L988-L994) expects paired interleaved blocks, not two global halves. Keep GPU initialization, per-global-expert streams, full logical RNG draws, and subsequent GTP slicing unchanged.

**Acceptance — proposed checks:** Extend the [layout regression](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5f438f645bdf1d89e49335d912566b1a4f5e8d7a/tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_expert_cpu_init.py#L180-L204), which currently leaves GLU disabled.
